content:
You are an autonomous agent working inside a Linux container, in a session with a user. The user's first request is in the first user message, and more requests arrive while you work. The user does not answer questions. When the session ends, automated tests check the final state of the container (files, programs, services), so the work must be done in the container, not just described.

## Session
The session lasts 30 minutes from the first message, then ends wherever you are. New user messages and subagent reports are delivered between your steps: a step is one response with its tool calls, and anything that arrives during a step waits until all of its tools have finished. A new request adds to the work: keep working on every earlier request unless the user says otherwise. A note after each step shows the time used and the subagents running. When you have nothing to do until a subagent report or a new user message arrives, call `wait`.

## Tools
- `spawn_subagents`: start subagents in the background (see Subagents below); it returns at once and each report arrives as a message.
- `wait`: pause until a subagent report or a new user message arrives (or timeout_sec passes); replying without a tool call also waits.
- `reply`: send a message to the user about one of their requests (see Replying to the user below).

You cannot run commands or change files yourself: everything that runs a command or modifies the container (building, testing, verifying included) must be delegated with `spawn_subagents`. You cannot read or search the files either: subagents read the code for you, so ask them for what you need to know.
Relative paths are resolved against your shell's current directory, which starts in /gin.

## Replying to the user
Every user message has an id (#3). The user reads only what you send with `reply(to, text, eta_min, done)`: your other text and your tool calls stay hidden from them. They want quick, correct answers to their questions, their bugs fixed, and to know when each fix will be ready.
- A question: answer it with `reply` (to its id). Answer from the code; a short answer is fine. Your first reply to a question is taken as your answer, so send it when you have the answer.
- A bug: in your first response after it arrives, reply with `eta_min`, your estimate of the minutes from now until it is fixed. Reply with a new `eta_min` whenever your estimate changes, and with `done: true` once it is fixed and checked.
- A status check: reply to each open bug with an updated `eta_min`.
- An urgent bug matters more than the earlier ones: fix it before them.

## Subagents
`spawn_subagents(instructions)` takes a list of instructions and starts one subagent per instruction in the background; the call returns at once. Subagents are separate model instances running in the SAME container as you. Each starts fresh: it sees only its instruction, not your conversation or the task, so make every instruction self-contained (goal, paths, commands, constraints, what to report). Each runs at most 2000 steps; its written report arrives as a message when it finishes, and you keep working (or `wait`) meanwhile. They share the filesystem with you and with each other, so give them independent work that does not edit the same files.

Your attention is the scarce resource: while your own tools run, new requests wait until they finish. Subagents run in the background, so delegate long work (investigating and fixing a bug, running a test suite) and keep yourself free to respond to new requests and to combine reports.

Scope: hard: subagents have `read_file`, `list_dir`, `search`, `bash` and `edit_file`; they can implement changes and verify them by running tests.

Limits: at most 60 subagents run at once; instructions beyond the free slots are not run. At most 60 subagent runs per episode; the budget left is shown after each step.

<instructions>
# Task

Your task is to fix all REPOSITORY DISCOVERABLE BUGS in repository given to you.
You MUST NOT make any OUT OF SCOPE edits.

## Definitions

### REPOSITORY

REPOSITORY means anything in the checked out working directory, including code,
and documentation.

### BUG

A bug is a behavior of the software that diverges from EXPECTED BEHAVIOR of it.

### REPOSITORY DISCOVERABLE BUG

A REPOSITORY DISCOVERABLE BUG is a bug whose source of EXPECTED BEHAVIOR is apparent to a reader of the REPOSITORY alone.
For the purposes of this classification, we only allow the ACCEPTED SOURCES OF EXPECTED BEHAVIOR and explicitly exclude any
OUT OF BAND KNOWLEDGE.

### ACCEPTED SOURCES OF EXPECTED BEHAVIOR

#### (1) User-facing documentation

The repository's own statements about itself that can be seen by the user and are therefore
assumed to be expected behavior by any user of the software project.

This includes documentation files and other parts of the repository that are turned into user-facing
documentation artifacts, such as docstrings or type annotations.

The repository may also incorporate an external source by reference, i.e.,
if a module states that it implements a named standard, that standard becomes
an in-repo contract.

Similarly, if in-repo contract sources claim to implement a mathematical function, or
a clearly established scientific concept, the code can be expected to stay true to
the mathematical/scientific expectation.

#### (2) Universally accepted expectations

Universally accepted expectations, e.g.,

- No segmentation faults in a C++ program. Note that other types of exceptions in e.g.,
  python, might be the excpted behavior (e.g., a ValueError in a library)
- No accidental deletion of user data.
- No freezes in a UI.
- No infinite loops.

The threshold for this category should be very high, i.e., you must be absolutely
sure that the expectation is universally shared by any user of this library.

### OUF OF BAND KNOWLEDGE

Knowledge not available from the two sources above.
This includes in particular:

- what the maintainers intended (unless evidenced by in-repo contracts)
- what an issue or PR text asserts,
- what users would want, and your own judgment that the old behavior was undesirable.

Your familiarity with this project from training is out of band.

### PRE-EXISTING TESTS

Pre-existing tests are the tests that are in the repository when you start.

### PRE-EXISTING GREEN TESTS

All PRE-EXISTING TESTS that are passing befor eyou make any edits

## OUT OF SCOPE

### Bugs only

You MUST NOT implement new features, changes, or enhancements.

### No modification to PRE-EXISTING TESTS

Do NOT edit or delete existing tests to make them pass.

### No failing of PRE-EXISTING GREEN TESTS

None of the PRE-EXISTING GREEN TESTS are allowed to be failing because of your changes.
Run the test suite at the beginning of your task and remember which tests are failing.
These are the only (!) PRE-EXISTING TESTS hhat are allowed to fail.
Breaking any (!) other PRE-EXISTING TEST will result in your score being set to zero.
This means that even if you found a clear, repository-evident bug, if fixing it breaks an existing test,
you MUST NOT do it.
Note that this even applies if any `Hint: ` section in the first user message explicitly points out
a bug, or information that points to it.
You must not, and under no circumstances, modify or make a pre-existing green test fail.
Instead, you should simply ignore these kinds of bugs.

## Settings

You are in a container. The REPOSITORY is checked out at `/gin`.

## Fairplay

This is a large task, but it IS (!) possible to solve.
You need to diligently work over a long time to achieve this task.
You must not break any rule because you deem the task too hard or too big.
If you are found to be breaking any fairplay rule, your score will be set to 0.

The following is considered to be cheating, a violation of fairplay:

- You must discover all bugs and fix them by looking at the source present only. Any way of gaining information about the
  "future" of this code (by looking in the internet, by poking around other installed versions etc.) is not allowed.
- You do not have internet access. You MUST NOT try to gain internet access.
- You MUST NOT attempt to gain access to source code other than the repository that is checked out at `/gin`.
- You MUST NOT use the size of the task to make excuses for "cheating"
</instructions>

Explore the code, find as many real bugs as you can, and fix them by editing the source files in place.

func TestZZTmpUnwrapProbe(t *testing.T) {
	inner := errors.New("inner")

	// (a) pointer form
	e := &Error{Err: inner, Type: ErrorTypePrivate}
	w := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", e)
	fmt.Println("=== (a) pointer form: e := &Error{...}; w := fmt.Errorf(\"wrapped: %w\", e) ===")
	fmt.Println("errors.Is(w, inner)      =", errors.Is(w, inner))
	fmt.Println("errors.Is(w, e)          =", errors.Is(w, e))
	fmt.Println("errors.Unwrap(e) == inner =", errors.Unwrap(e) == inner, "(Unwrap(e) =", errors.Unwrap(e), ")")
	var ptr *Error
	asPtr := errors.As(w, &ptr)
	fmt.Println("errors.As(w, &ptr)       =", asPtr, "ptr =", ptr)

	// (b) value form
	ev := Error{Err: inner, Type: ErrorTypePrivate}
	wv := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", ev)
	fmt.Println("=== (b) value form: ev := Error{...}; wv := fmt.Errorf(\"wrapped: %w\", ev) ===")
	fmt.Println("errors.Is(wv, inner)     =", errors.Is(wv, inner))
	fmt.Println("errors.Is(wv, ev)        =", errors.Is(wv, ev))
	unwrappedEv := errors.Unwrap(ev)
	fmt.Println("errors.Unwrap(ev)        =", unwrappedEv)
	_, evHasUnwrap := any(ev).(interface{ Unwrap() error })
	fmt.Println("ev implements interface{ Unwrap() error } =", evHasUnwrap)
	_, evPtrHasUnwrap := any(&ev).(interface{ Unwrap() error })
	fmt.Println("&ev implements interface{ Unwrap() error } =", evPtrHasUnwrap)
	var val Error
	asVal := errors.As(wv, &val)
	fmt.Println("errors.As(wv, &val)      =", asVal, "val =", val)

	// (c) does the value type implement error?
	fmt.Println("=== (c) error interface satisfaction ===")
	var x error = Error{}
	fmt.Println("var x error = Error{}; x =", x)
	var y error = &Error{}
	fmt.Println("var y error = &Error{}; y =", y)

	// (d) errors.Is directly on the value
	fmt.Println("=== (d) errors.Is(ev, inner) directly on value ===")
	fmt.Println("errors.Is(ev, inner)     =", errors.Is(ev, inner))
}

## 2) What `setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles` returns when `value.Len() != len(files)`

Exact code (lines 63–74, full function including loop and trailing returns):

```go
func setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles(value reflect.Value, field reflect.StructField, files []*multipart.FileHeader) (isSet bool, err error) {
	if value.Len() != len(files) {
		return false, ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid
	}
	for i := range files {
		set, err := setByMultipartFormFile(value.Index(i), field, files[i:i+1])
		if err != nil || !set {
			return set, err
		}
	}
	return true, nil
}
```

Answer: on the length mismatch it returns **`false` (isSet == false) and a non-nil error `ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid`** — i.e. `(false, ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid)`. It does **not** return nil. `ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid` is the package-level sentinel defined at line 23: `errors.New("unsupported len of array for []*multipart.FileHeader")` (exported, so callers can compare with `errors.Is`). The loop is not executed in that case (early return); the only other returns are `return set, err` inside the loop (propagating a nested failure, where `set` may be false and `err` may be nil if the element setter returned `(false, nil)`) and the final `return true, nil` after a fully successful loop.

## 3) Signatures of the functions in that file

- `type multipartRequest http.Request` (line 14); `var _ setter = (*multipartRequest)(nil)` (line 16) — implements the `setter` interface from binding/form_mapping.go:63: `TrySet(value reflect.Value, field reflect.StructField, key string, opt setOptions) (isSet bool, err error)`.
- `func (r *multipartRequest) TrySet(value reflect.Value, field reflect.StructField, key string, opt setOptions) (bool, error)` (line 27) — returns `(bool, error)`. If `r.MultipartForm.File[key]` is non-empty it delegates to `setByMultipartFormFile(value, field, files)`; otherwise it falls back to `setByForm(value, field, r.MultipartForm.Value, key, opt)` (form_mapping.go:167).
- `func setByMultipartFormFile(value reflect.Value, field reflect.StructField, files []*multipart.FileHeader) (isSet bool, err error)` (line 35) — returns `(bool, error)`. Handles `reflect.Ptr` → `*multipart.FileHeader` (sets `files[0]`, returns `true, nil`), `reflect.Struct` → `multipart.FileHeader` (sets `*files[0]`, returns `true, nil`), `reflect.Slice` (makes a slice of `len(files)`, calls `setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles`, and only assigns `value.Set(slice)` if `err == nil && isSet`, else returns `(isSet, err)`), `reflect.Array` (direct `return setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles(value, field, files)`). Default fallthrough: `return false, ErrMultiFileHeader` (line 60).
- `func setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles(value reflect.Value, field reflect.StructField, files []*multipart.FileHeader) (isSet bool, err error)` (line 63) — returns `(bool, error)` as described in (2).

Note: there is no `setMultipartForm` / `setMultipartFormFiles` function in this repo — the only helpers are the three above (grep over all `*.go` confirms `setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles` is referenced only at lines 51 and 58, and `setByMultipartFormFile` only at lines 29 and 68). `ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid` is defined and returned but never referenced in any `_test.go` file (grep found no test usage).

## 3) Type / fields / all methods

Type + fields (response_writer.go:46-50): `type responseWriter struct { http.ResponseWriter; size int; status int }` — embedded `http.ResponseWriter` (promotes Header(), and is the delegate for Write/WriteHeader), plus exactly two extra fields: `size int` (bytes written; sentinel `noWritten = -1` means "not written yet") and `status int` (intended status code; initialized to `defaultStatus = http.StatusOK`). There is no separate `written bool` field — "written" is derived from `size != noWritten`. Interface assertion `var _ ResponseWriter = &responseWriter{}` at line 52.

Methods (full bodies are verbatim in section 1): `reset(writer http.ResponseWriter)` (54-58), `WriteHeader(code int)` (60-67), `WriteHeaderNow()` (69-74), `Write(data []byte) (n int, err error)` (76-81), `WriteString(s string) (n int, err error)` (83-88), `Status() int` (90-92), `Size() int` (94-96), `Written() bool` (98-100), `Hijack() (net.Conn, *bufio.ReadWriter, error)` (103-108), `CloseNotify() <-chan bool` (111-113), `Flush()` (116-119), `Pusher() (pusher http.Pusher)` (121-126). Header() is not overridden (promoted from the embedded writer). The `ResponseWriter` interface (20-44) additionally requires Status, Size, WriteString, Written, WriteHeaderNow, Pusher, and embeds http.ResponseWriter/Hijacker/Flusher/CloseNotifier.

## 4) `status` field analysis

- Set in `reset`: `w.status = defaultStatus` (200). Never set anywhere else in this file except `WriteHeader`.
- Set in `WriteHeader(code int)`: yes, but only when `code > 0 && w.status != code` (line 61-66). It does NOT touch the underlying writer (no `ResponseWriter.WriteHeader` call) — it only records the intent, and logs a `debugPrint` warning if headers were already flushed. `WriteHeader(-1)` (or 0) is silently ignored, so the previous status is kept.
- Set in `Write()`: no. `Write` calls `w.WriteHeaderNow()` (which flushes `w.status` to the underlying writer, defaulting to 200) and then delegates. Same for `WriteString`. This is correct and intentional: HTTP defaults to 200 when no header was set, and `w.status` is already 200 from `reset`, so `Status()` returns 200 in that case. The test `TestResponseWriterWrite` asserts exactly this (`w.Status() == http.StatusOK`, `testWriter.Code == http.StatusOK`). So "status not updated when Write is called without WriteHeader" is NOT a defect here — the default value covers it.
- `Status()` exists (line 90-92) and returns `w.status`, i.e. the intended/recorded code, not necessarily what is on the wire yet. `TestResponseWriterWriteHeader` relies on this: after `WriteHeader(300)`, `w.Status()==300` while `testWriter.Code` is still its untouched zero value (200 for httptest.NewRecorder's Code field default). `Status()` is also used by gin.go:656 in `serveError`.
- Related invariants: `Written()` is `size != noWritten`; `WriteHeaderNow()` sets `size = 0` and writes `w.status` only if not yet written; `Hijack()` marks written (`if w.size < 0 { w.size = 0 }`); `Flush()` forces `WriteHeaderNow()` first. `Size()` returns -1 before anything is written.
- Direct external mutation of the field exists: gin.go:651 `c.writermem.status = code` in `serveError` (bypasses WriteHeader, intentional to force an error status before handlers run).

Conclusion for item 4: I found no inconsistency in response_writer.go. The status handling (default 200, recorded by WriteHeader, flushed by WriteHeaderNow/Write/WriteString/Flush, read by Status) matches upstream gin v1.8.1 exactly, and the file reads as unmodified upstream code. Note the test file has no coverage for `WriteString`, `Pusher`, or for `Status()` after `WriteHeaderNow` (only the underlying `testWriter.Code` is checked there); the TODO comment at lines 15-18 is stale (tests for Hijack/CloseNotify/Flush do exist below it).

## 2) Exact body of `SetMode` (lines 56–77)

```go
func SetMode(value string) {
	if value == "" {
		if flag.Lookup("test.v") != nil {
			value = TestMode
		} else {
			value = DebugMode
		}
	}

	switch value {
	case DebugMode:
		ginMode = debugCode
	case ReleaseMode:
		ginMode = releaseCode
	case TestMode:
		ginMode = testCode
	default:
		panic("gin mode unknown: " + value + " (available mode: debug release test)")
	}

	modeName = value
}
```

**`value == ""` and `flag.Lookup("test.v") == nil` (not under `go test`):** the `if value == ""` branch is entered, the inner `flag.Lookup("test.v") != nil` is false, so the `else` runs: `value = DebugMode` — i.e. `value` is reassigned to the string `"debug"`. The `switch` then matches `case DebugMode`, so `ginMode = debugCode` (the constant `0`, since `debugCode = iota` is the first in the block at lines 27–31). Finally `modeName = value`, so `modeName` holds `"debug"`. **No panic occurs** — the `default` arm is never reached because `value` is no longer `""`. Net effect: `gin.Mode()` returns `"debug"`. (This is also what happens at package init when `GIN_MODE` is unset: `init()` at line 50–53 calls `SetMode(os.Getenv(EnvGinMode))` with `""`.)

## 3) Other cases

- **`value == ""` and `test.v` IS present (under `go test`):** `flag.Lookup("test.v") != nil` is true, so `value = TestMode` (`"test"`); the switch matches `case TestMode` → `ginMode = testCode` (`2`); `modeName = "test"`; no panic. `gin.Mode()` returns `"test"`.
- **Unknown mode string (e.g. `"bogus"`):** the `value == ""` block is skipped, no `case` matches, so the `default` arm runs: `panic("gin mode unknown: " + value + " (available mode: debug release test)")` — e.g. `panic: gin mode unknown: bogus (available mode: debug release test)`. Because the panic happens before line 76, `modeName` and `ginMode` keep their previous values (initially `"debug"` / `debugCode`).

## Answer (READ-ONLY; no files in /gin modified by me)

**`source` does NOT return a string — it returns `[]byte`.** Its exact signature is:

```go
func source(lines [][]byte, n int) []byte
```

Verbatim body (recovery.go lines 136–143, from `cat -n recovery.go`):

```go
136	// source returns a space-trimmed slice of the n'th line.
137	func source(lines [][]byte, n int) []byte {
138		n-- // in stack trace, lines are 1-indexed but our array is 0-indexed
139		if n < 0 || n >= len(lines) {
140			return dunno
141		}
142		return bytes.TrimSpace(lines[n])
143	}
```

Package-level `dunno` (lines 23–28):

```go
23	var (
24		dunno     = []byte("???")
25		centerDot = []byte("·")
26		dot       = []byte(".")
27		slash     = []byte("/")
28	)
```

### The two cases
Note `n--` happens **before** the guard, so the guard tests `n-1`:

- **`n < 0`** (e.g. `-1`, `-5`): after `n--` it is still `< 0` → returns the package var `dunno`, i.e. the byte slice `[]byte("???")` (string `"???"`). No panic.
- **`n >= len(lines)`** (e.g. `n == len(lines)`, `n == 10`): after `n--` it is `>= len(lines)` → also returns `dunno` = `[]byte("???")`. No panic.
- In-bounds `1 <= n <= len(lines)`: returns `bytes.TrimSpace(lines[n-1])` (whitespace-trimmed slice of that line).

### Verification (ran in container, go1.18.10)
`go test -run 'TestSource|TestFunction' -v ./` → `TestSource PASS`, `TestFunction PASS`, `TestFunctionName PASS`, `ok github.com/gin-gonic/gin 0.010s`.

Temporary probe test (created, run, then deleted — `ls zz_src_probe_test.go` → No such file; `git status` clean for recovery.go) printed:

```
source(in, 0)  = "???"      // in = [][]byte{"Hello world.", "Hi, gin.."}
source(in, -1) = "???"
source(in, -5) = "???"
source(in, 1)  = "Hello world."
source(in, 2)  = "Hi, gin.."
source(in, 3)  = "???"
source(in, 10) = "???"
source(nil, 0) = "???"
source(nil, -1)= "???"
dunno          = "???"
```

Existing repo test `recovery_test.go:93-106` (`TestSource`) asserts the same: `source(nil, 0) == dunno`, `source(in, 10) == dunno`, `source(in, 1) == []byte("Hello world.")`.

### Other helpers in recovery.go (exact signatures + behaviour)
- `func stack(skip int) []byte` (line 110): builds a formatted stack trace in a `bytes.Buffer`; loops `i := skip` upward calling `runtime.Caller(i)`, breaking when `!ok`. Per frame writes `fmt.Fprintf(buf, "%s:%d (0x%x)\n", file, line, pc)`; caches file contents with `ioutil.ReadFile(file)` + `bytes.Split(data, []byte{'\n'})` into `lines` keyed by `lastFile` (on read error it `continue`s, so no source line is printed); then writes `fmt.Fprintf(buf, "\t%s: %s\n", function(pc), source(lines, line))`. Returns `buf.Bytes()`.
- `func function(pc uintptr) []byte` (line 146): `fn := runtime.FuncForPC(pc)`; if `fn == nil` returns `dunno`. Else takes `[]byte(fn.Name())`, strips everything up to and including the last `/` (`bytes.LastIndex(name, slash)`), then everything up to and including the first `.` (`bytes.Index(name, dot)`), then `bytes.Replace(name, centerDot, dot, -1)` (replaces `·` with `.`). Returns the shortened name.
- `func timeFormat(t time.Time) string` (line 171): returns `t.Format("2006/01/02 - 15:04:05")`.
- Middleware helpers: `type RecoveryFunc func(c *Context, err any)` (line 31); `Recovery() HandlerFunc` → `RecoveryWithWriter(DefaultErrorWriter)`; `CustomRecovery(handle RecoveryFunc) HandlerFunc` → `RecoveryWithWriter(DefaultErrorWriter, handle)`; `RecoveryWithWriter(out io.Writer, recovery ...RecoveryFunc) HandlerFunc` (uses `recovery[0]` if len>0, else `defaultHandleRecovery`); `CustomRecoveryWithWriter(out io.Writer, handle RecoveryFunc) HandlerFunc` (logger prefix `"\n\n\x1b[31m"`, `log.LstdFlags`; detects broken pipe via `*net.OpError`/`*os.SyscallError` containing "broken pipe" or "connection reset by peer"; masks `Authorization` header; calls `stack(3)`); `func defaultHandleRecovery(c *Context, err any)` → `c.AbortWithStatus(http.StatusInternalServerError)`.

func TestContextRenderRedirectAll(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := CreateTestContext(httptest.NewRecorder())
	c.Request, _ = http.NewRequest("POST", "http://example.com", nil)
	assert.Panics(t, func() { c.Redirect(http.StatusOK, "/resource") })
	assert.Panics(t, func() { c.Redirect(http.StatusAccepted, "/resource") })
	assert.Panics(t, func() { c.Redirect(299, "/resource") })
	assert.Panics(t, func() { c.Redirect(309, "/resource") })
	assert.NotPanics(t, func() { c.Redirect(http.StatusMultipleChoices, "/resource") })
	assert.NotPanics(t, func() { c.Redirect(http.StatusPermanentRedirect, "/resource") })
}

func TestContextNegotiationWithJSON(t *testing.T) {
	w := httptest.NewRecorder()
	c, _ := CreateTestContext(w)
	c.Request, _ = http.NewRequest("POST", "", nil)

	c.Negotiate(http.StatusOK, Negotiate{
		Offered: []string{MIMEJSON, MIMEXML, MIMEYAML},
		Data:    H{"foo": "bar"},
	})

	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, w.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, "{\"foo\":\"bar\"}", w.Body.String())
	assert.Equal(t, "application/json; charset=utf-8", w.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
}

func TestContextNegotiationFormatWithWildcardAccept(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := CreateTestContext(httptest.NewRecorder())
	c.Request, _ = http.NewRequest("POST", "/", nil)
	c.Request.Header.Add("Accept", "*/*")

	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat("*/*"), "*/*")
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat("text/*"), "text/*")
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat("application/*"), "application/*")
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEJSON), MIMEJSON)
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEXML), MIMEXML)
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEHTML), MIMEHTML)

	c, _ = CreateTestContext(httptest.NewRecorder())
	c.Request, _ = http.NewRequest("POST", "/", nil)
	c.Request.Header.Add("Accept", "text/*")

	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat("*/*"), "*/*")
	assert.Equal(t, c.NegotiateFormat("text/*"), "text/*")

func TestContextNegotiationFormatCustom(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := CreateTestContext(httptest.NewRecorder())
	c.Request, _ = http.NewRequest("POST", "/", nil)
	c.Request.Header.Add("Accept", "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9;q=0.8")

	c.Accepted = nil
	c.SetAccepted(MIMEJSON, MIMEXML)

	assert.Equal(t, MIMEJSON, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEJSON, MIMEXML))
	assert.Equal(t, MIMEXML, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEXML, MIMEHTML))
	assert.Equal(t, MIMEJSON, c.NegotiateFormat(MIMEJSON))
}

func TestContextIsAborted(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := CreateTestContext(httptest.NewRecorder())
	assert.False(t, c.IsAborted())

	assert.True(t, c.IsAborted())

	c.Next()
	assert.True(t, c.IsAborted())
